With treatment with fluconazole in a single dose of 150 mg, there are some data suggesting that the warfarin concentration and INR will increase, but the magnitude is uncertain and appears to vary from patient to patient. In a small study, INR increased by an average of 30-40 % (for example from a baseline value of 2,0 up to 2,8, or from 2,5 up to 3,3) on day 5, when the effect on INR was maximal. Eight days after fluconazole intake, INR levels had returned to normal. However, some patients had INR values above 4 on day 5, whereas the effect was minimal in others.

With treatment with fluconazole at a fixed daily dose over several days, the concentration of warfarin will increase, with an associated increased risk of bleeding. The effect is dose-dependent: At a fluconazole dose of 100 mg/d, the warfarin concentration increases by an average of 30 %, at a dose of 200 mg/d it increases by 70 %, and at a dose of 400 mg/d up to a doubling of the warfarin concentration is seen. The effect on INR will be far greater than this.
